name: Logo
description: The logo shows the product’s mark and name, usually at the start of the navigation bar, linking to the home page. Its colors, corners and spacing follow the theme.
whenToUse: At the start of the Navbar, linking home.
In sign-in screens, footers and empty states that name the product.

anatomy.name: Mark
anatomy.description: Icon on a brand-colored tile; corners follow the radius theme.

anatomy.name: Name
anatomy.description: The wordmark; also the accessible name.

values.meaning: Mark only, for tight spaces; the name is still announced.

states.name: Focus
states.meaning: A linked logo shows the focus ring.

behavior.text: With href the logo is a single link named by the product name.
Brand, mode, radius and density come from the theme; there are no brand props. Wrap in ThemeProvider to show another brand.

content: Use the product name exactly as it is written in the brand.

guidelines.do: Link the logo to the home page.
guidelines.dont: Add a separate “Home” link next to it that does the same.
guidelines.why: People expect the logo to go home; a duplicate link adds noise.

guidelines.do: Keep the name visible where there’s room.
guidelines.dont: Hide the name everywhere to look minimal.
guidelines.why: The name tells new visitors where they are.

guidelines.do: Let the theme color the logo.
guidelines.dont: Override its colors per brand in page CSS.
guidelines.why: Theme tokens keep contrast right in every brand and mode.

accessibility.role: link (with href), img (name hidden) or plain text.

keyboard.action: Reach and follow a linked logo.

aria.when: Set to the name when hideName is on.

accessibility.focus: A linked logo shows the focus ring.

wcag.how: The name is always the text alternative.
The link is named by the product name.

examples.title: Home link
examples.description: The usual case, at the start of the Navbar.

examples.title: Mark only
examples.description: For narrow layouts; still named for screen readers.
examples.code:
import { Logo } from '@ds/react';

<Logo name="TechHub" hideName href="/" />

examples.title: In another brand
examples.code:
import { Logo, ThemeProvider } from '@ds/react';

<ThemeProvider theme={{ brand: 'amber' }}>
  <Logo name="TechHub" />
</ThemeProvider>

related.relation: The logo usually starts the navigation bar.

changes: name replaces text; href makes it a link; hideName shows the mark only.
brand, radius, density and language props removed: the theme sets them. Hard-coded colors removed.
Default mark is a Lucide icon instead of a Font Awesome class.

components.name: Logo
components.description: The product's mark and name. Colors, corners and spacing follow the theme.

name.description: Product or company name. Shown as the wordmark and used as the accessible name.

icon.description: The mark, usually an icon. Decorative: the name already says what it is.

href.description: Makes the logo a link, usually to the home page.

hideName.description: Shows only the mark, e.g. in tight spaces. The name is still announced.

--logo-icon-bg-color.description: Solid fill for emphasized actions of a tone, e.g. filled buttons.

--logo-icon-color.description: Text and icons on the matching --color-bg-accent fill.

--logo-name-font-family.description: Body text and most UI text.

--logo-focus-ring-width.description: Thickness of the keyboard focus ring.

--logo-focus-ring-offset.description: Gap between an element and its focus ring.

--logo-focus-ring-color.description: Focus ring color; follows the brand accent.

--logo-gap.description: Spacing steps in px (see --spacing-* in themes/density.css).

--logo-icon-border-radius.description: Corner radius steps in px (see --radius-* in themes/radius.css).

--logo-name-font-content.description: Translated demo text. Real components take text from props, not tokens.
